title: Caribbean Guava-Lime Barbecue Sauce
description: Pink guava makes a velvety barbecue sauce with lime, sweet smoked paprika and a dark ribbon of molasses.

ingredients.name: unsweetened seedless guava puree
ingredients.note: Use thawed GOYA guava pulp without added sugar or salt, measured by volume.

ingredients.name: table salt
ingredients.note: Fine table salt, about 590 mg sodium per 1/4 teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/16 tsp total.

steps.title: Loosen the guava
steps.text: Whisk {gv}, {w} and {to} in the HexClad over medium-low heat until the fruit is completely smooth.

steps.title: Concentrate the fruit
steps.text: Stir in {mo}, {pa}, {cv} and {salt}. Simmer uncovered for 7–10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with lime
steps.text: Fold in {lj} off the heat to keep the lime bright.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Brush over warm pork slices or spoon alongside shrimp. A small spoonful also works on soft sweet potatoes.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/16 tsp table salt in place of 1/4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, skip the cider vinegar and cut the lime juice to 1 teaspoon. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 26 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 6.2 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 2.0 g fiber, 151 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 26 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 6.2 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 2.0 g fiber, 41 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.

steps.title: Set up the cooking vessel
steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
